newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch money rates driven higher by tightness.
newsitem.headline: Dutch money rates driven higher by tightness.

text.p: Dutch money rates nudged higher on Tuesday, with dealers saying that call money rates could ease somewhat after the allocation of liquiditity under a new special advances pact on Thursday.
"The current allocation was too tight," said one dealer, adding that early tax payments had contributed to the scarcity of funds.

Guilder-deposits also rose a few basis points as the market digested the idea that official rates in Germany were not likely to fall any more and the approach of the end of the year had also put some upward pressure on rates.

Several remarks from Bundesbank officials in recent weeks have left the market with the idea that official rates will not drop any further, although dealers said the comments have not been very consistent.

Earlier today, Bundebank council member Sievert said it was not yet clear whether the rate cut cycle had bottomed out and his remarks were soon followed by those of another council member, Koebrick, who said there was no need to change the discount, lombard and repo rates.
Last week Buba's Issing also made some pronouncements about German interest rates.
"It just leaves us with a lot of uncertainty," said another dealer who said he had stopped listening to all the remarks and had concluded the next move in German rates would be up.
Call money rates added six basis points to 2.87 percent bid.
One month deposits gained four basis points to 2.86 percent bid and three month paper rose to 2.88 percent bid from 2.86 percent.
Forward rate agreements (FRAs) were up and some dealers said this could indicate that all rates were likely to rise further.
The guilder was slightly weaker against the mark at 112.175 per 100 marks from 112.155 on Monday.
